Clause 1 (every bounded directed D ⊆ sa(𝒜) has a supremum ⋁D in sa(𝒜)) is the field isLUB_of_bddAbove_directed; clause 2 (the normal positive functionals are faithful: 0 ≤ a and ω a = 0 for every np-functional ω forces a = 0) is the field np_faithful; the notation ⋁D that clause 1 introduces is dirSup, with isLUB_dirSup for its defining property. The footnote (centre separating would already suffice) is a remark and is deliberately not rendered. Two deviations, both benign. column6: the definition of an np-functional (vn.tex:196-205, def-np-functional), never rowed until now, checked clause by clause. 'Positive linear map ω : 𝒜 → ℂ' is the extended Mathlib PositiveLinearMap 𝒜 →ₚ[ℂ] ℂ, i.e. ℂ-linear plus monotone; for a linear map between ordered groups monotone and positivity-preserving are the same condition, so this is the printed hypothesis and not a strengthening. 'Normal' is the field preservesDirSups', unfolding to PreservesDirSups (Common.lean:37), which for nonempty directed D with IsLUB D s asserts IsLUB (ω '' D) (ω s) -- the printed ω(⋁D) = ⋁_{d∈D} ω(d), with the existence of the right-hand side asserted rather than presupposed, which is the reading the printed equation carries. The image supremum is taken in ℂ under ComplexOrder, but an upper bound in ℂ of a set of reals is real, so it is the supremum in ℝ that ⋁_{d∈D} ω(d) means. Two deviations, both benign. (i) D.Nonempty is added, as in 42I. (ii) The printed condition quantifies over bounded directed D having a supremum, PreservesDirSups over all directed D having a supremum, which is formally the larger class (IsLUB D s gives BddAbove D but not norm-boundedness). The two conditions on ω are equivalent: given directed D with ⋁D = s, pick d₀ ∈ D and put D' = D ∩ [d₀,∞), which is directed, cofinal in D, contained in [d₀,s] and hence norm-bounded, with ⋁D' = s; and since ω is monotone and D' cofinal, ω '' D and ω '' D' have the same upper bounds. So NPFunctional is exactly the printed class and not a subclass of it. No boundedness or continuity is bundled, matching the thesis, where automatic boundedness of a positive functional and the equivalence of normality with ultraweak continuity (44XV, p-uwcont) are theorems rather than parts of the definition. column6: 54XI's normality clause -- the 'n' of 'nmiu-isomorphism' (vn.tex:2036) -- at full generality: any L-infinity-presentation q of a C*-algebra that is surjective, additive, multiplicative and star-preserving with kernel exactly the mu-a.e.-zero functions carries a least upper bound for the a.e. order on bounded measurable functions to a least upper bound in the algebra. So normality is AUTOMATIC from the other presentation clauses; it did not have to be built into the construction. Two things about the shape are deliberate and worth recording. (i) DIRECTEDNESS IS NOT ASSUMED and is not needed: by linftyPresentation_le_iff together with surjectivity q is an order isomorphism modulo a.e. equality, so it preserves whichever suprema exist -- the directed ones PreservesDirSups asks about among them. The clause is therefore stronger than PreservesDirSups would be. (ii) It is stated of q rather than of the thesis's f maps-to f-circle because q is that map's inverse in the presentation convention, and normality transfers across an order isomorphism. Proof route is ours, not the thesis's: the thesis says normality is automatic for an nmiu-isomorphism and leaves it there
